lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: James: overview
nodes.d: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?
ev: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written

nodes.t: Trials, wisdom and the crown of life
nodes.d: James says to count trials as joy because tested faith produces patience, to ask God for wisdom without wavering, and promises the crown of life to the one who endures.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James says to count it all joy when trials come?
ev: Explain what testing of faith produces
Say how James tells believers to ask for wisdom

nodes.t: Temptation, the word and doing it
nodes.d: James says God does not tempt anyone; desire gives birth to sin and sin to death, while every good gift comes from the Father of lights who gave new birth by the word of truth, and believers must be doers of the word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the difference between hearing the word and doing it?
ev: Describe the path from desire to death in 1:14-15
Contrast hearing the word with doing it
State what James calls pure religion

nodes.t: No partiality: the royal law
nodes.d: James rebukes giving the rich seats of honour and shaming the poor in the assembly, reminds them God chose the poor rich in faith, and calls loving your neighbour the royal law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what James says is wrong with favouring the rich over the poor?
ev: Describe the example of partiality in the assembly
Say what James calls the royal law
Explain why partiality is sin according to 2:9

nodes.t: Faith and works
nodes.d: James argues that faith without works is dead, using the demons who believe, Abraham offering Isaac, and Rahab, and concludes a man is justified by works and not by faith only.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James is arguing about the kind of faith that is dead?
ev: Explain what James means by faith that is alone and dead
Retell how Abraham and Rahab are used as examples
Compare the wording of James 2:24 with Romans 3:28 and 4:2-3

nodes.t: The tongue
nodes.d: James warns that few should be teachers, compares the tongue to a bit, a rudder and a fire, and says it cannot be tamed by man yet is used both to bless God and curse people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say why James calls the tongue a fire?
ev: Name the three pictures James uses for the tongue
Say what inconsistency James points out in 3:9-10

nodes.t: Wisdom from above and earthly wisdom
nodes.d: James contrasts envy and strife, which he calls earthly, sensual and devilish wisdom, with wisdom from above, which is pure, peaceable, gentle and full of mercy and good fruits.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how to tell wisdom from above from earthly wisdom?
ev: List the marks of wisdom from above
Describe what comes with bitter envying and strife

nodes.t: Conflicts, the world and humbling before God
nodes.d: James traces fightings to desires within, calls friendship with the world enmity with God, and says God gives grace to the humble, so believers must submit, resist the devil and draw near to God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do instead of fighting and loving the world?
ev: Say where James says wars and fightings come from
List the commands in 4:7-10
Explain what God does with the proud and the humble

nodes.t: Judging others and boasting about tomorrow
nodes.d: James forbids speaking evil of a brother and judging him since there is one lawgiver, and rebukes plans made without saying if the Lord will, since life is a vapour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James says to say, If the Lord will?
ev: Say why James says there is one lawgiver
Explain what James says we should say about our plans
State the point of 4:17

nodes.t: Warning to the rich who defraud
nodes.d: James tells rich men to weep for coming miseries: their riches are corrupted, wages withheld from labourers cry out to the Lord of sabaoth, and they have lived in luxury and condemned the just.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the rich are accused of in James 5:1-6?
ev: Name the charges James brings against the rich in 5:1-6
Say who hears the cries of the harvest labourers

nodes.t: Patience until the coming of the Lord
nodes.d: James urges patience like the farmer waiting for rain, points to the prophets and Job as examples, says the Lord is pitiful and merciful, and tells them not to swear oaths.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James says to be patient until the coming of the Lord?
ev: Describe the farmer picture of patience
Name the examples of endurance James gives
Say what James tells them about oaths

nodes.t: Prayer, healing and restoring the wanderer
nodes.d: James tells the afflicted to pray, the sick to call the elders, believers to confess faults and pray for one another, cites Elijah as a man like us whose prayer was answered, and ends by urging restoring one who strays from the truth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James says to do when someone is sick, sinning or wandering?
ev: Describe what the sick are told to do in 5:14-15
Say how James uses Elijah
Explain what happens when someone turns a sinner from error

nodes.t: Genesis: overview
nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.t: Abram believed and it was counted as righteousness
nodes.d: Genesis 15:6 records that Abram believed the LORD and it was counted to him as righteousness, the verse Paul explains in Romans 4.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Genesis 15:6 in their own words?
ev: Quote or paraphrase 15:6 accurately
Say who or what Abram believed

nodes.t: Abraham offers Isaac
nodes.d: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac; God provides a ram in his place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God provided on the mountain?
ev: Retell the story, including 22:8 and 22:13-14

nodes.t: The Ten Commandments
nodes.d: God speaks all these words, beginning by saying he is the LORD who brought Israel out of Egypt. They cover having no other gods, no images, not taking his name in vain, remembering the sabbath, honouring father and mother, and not killing, committing adultery, stealing, bearing false witness or coveting.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say the Ten Commandments in order and say what comes before them in 20:2?
ev: Recite the ten commandments in order from the Bible
Say what 20:2 says before the commandments begin
Say the reason given for the sabbath (20:11)

nodes.t: Leviticus: overview
nodes.d: Leviticus gives the LORD's instructions from the tabernacle: the offerings, the consecration of the priests, clean and unclean, the day of atonement, holy living, the feasts, the jubilee, and the blessings and curses of obedience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a one-sentence summary of what Leviticus is about?
ev: Name the main sections of Leviticus (offerings, priests, clean and unclean, atonement, holiness, feasts, jubilee, blessings and curses).

nodes.t: "Ye shall be holy": laws for neighbours
nodes.d: Leviticus 19 gathers commands under the call to be holy because the LORD is holy: honouring parents, sabbaths, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, no partiality, loving one's neighbour as oneself, care for the stranger and just weights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some ways Leviticus 19 says holiness shows up in daily life?
ev: Name at least five commands from the chapter that deal with how to treat other people.
Find the command to love the neighbour (19:18) and the command about the stranger (19:33-34).

nodes.t: Joshua: overview
nodes.d: Joshua records Israel crossing the Jordan after Moses' death (1:1-2), taking and dividing the land, and Joshua's closing call to serve the LORD at Shechem, ending with his death (24:29).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Joshua from the crossing of the Jordan to the covenant at Shechem?
ev: Say how the book begins with the death of Moses and ends with the death of Joshua
Name the three parts: entering and conquering, dividing the land, and the farewell charges

nodes.t: Rahab hides the spies in Jericho
nodes.d: Joshua sends two men to Jericho, where Rahab hides them, confesses that the LORD is God in heaven and earth, and secures their oath to spare her family, marked by a scarlet cord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Rahab did for the spies and what they promised her?
ev: Retell how Rahab hid the spies
Say what Rahab had heard about the LORD (2:9-11)
Describe the promise the men made and the sign of the scarlet line (2:12-21)

nodes.t: 1 Kings: overview
nodes.d: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?
ev: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)

nodes.t: Elijah announces drought and is fed by ravens
nodes.d: Elijah the Tishbite tells Ahab there will be neither dew nor rain except by his word, and the LORD sends him to hide by the brook Cherith, where ravens bring him bread and flesh until the brook dries up.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God provided for Elijah by the brook Cherith?
ev: Say what Elijah told Ahab (17:1)
Explain how the LORD fed Elijah at Cherith

nodes.t: The rain returns
nodes.d: Elijah tells Ahab to eat, because there is the sound of abundance of rain; after he prays and his servant looks seven times, a small cloud rises and heavy rain falls.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the drought ended in Elijah's day?
ev: Say what Elijah's servant saw on the seventh look (18:44)
Explain what this ended (compare 17:1)

nodes.t: Job: overview
nodes.d: Job opens with a righteous man losing everything (1-2), moves through his lament and long exchanges with three friends (3-31), Elihu (32-37) and the LORD answering from the whirlwind (38-41), and ends with Job’s repentance and restoration (42).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Job in four or five parts and name who speaks in each?
ev: Outline the book of Job in its main parts: prologue, speeches, the LORD’s answer, epilogue.

nodes.t: The LORD restores Job and rebukes the friends
nodes.d: The LORD says the three friends have not spoken of him rightly as Job has, tells them to offer a burnt offering with Job praying for them, and then gives Job twice as much as before, seven sons and three daughters, and many more years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD tells the friends to do, and what happens to Job at the end?
ev: State why the LORD is angry with Eliphaz and his friends (42:7).
List what the LORD gives Job in 42:10-16.

nodes.t: Proverbs: overview
nodes.d: Proverbs begins with the proverbs of Solomon son of David (1:1), sets out a father’s teaching about wisdom and folly (1-9), gathers many short sayings (10-29), and ends with the words of Agur (30) and of king Lemuel (31).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the main sections of Proverbs and who is named as the source of each?
ev: Describe the main sections of Proverbs: 1-9, 10-22, 22-24, 25-29, 30, 31.

nodes.t: Trust in the LORD with all your heart
nodes.d: The father tells his son to keep his commandments, trust in the LORD and not lean on his own understanding, accept the LORD’s correction, value wisdom above silver and gold, and do good to his neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Proverbs 3:5-6 and give one example of leaning on one’s own understanding?
ev: Read 3:5-6 and say what the son is told to do and what the LORD does.
Find 3:11-12 and say what it says about correction.

nodes.t: Justification by faith
nodes.d: The righteousness of God is through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe; we are justified freely by his grace through the redemption in Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Romans 3:21-26 says a sinner is justified?
ev: Explain "justified freely by his grace" (3:24)
Say what propitiation means in 3:25 in the passage's context
